title: must, mustn't, needn't
subtitle: You must / You mustn't / You needn't
summary: Tell apart mustn't (don't do it) and needn't (it's not necessary), and use needn't have (done) for something you did that was not necessary.

lesson.heading: must and mustn't
lesson.text: **You must do something** = it is necessary that you do it. **You mustn't do something** = don't do it.

examples.text: Don't tell anybody what I said. You **must keep** it a secret.
We don't have much time. We **must hurry**.
You must keep it a secret. You **mustn't tell** anyone.
We must be very quiet. We **mustn't make** any noise.

lesson.heading: needn't and don't need to
lesson.text: **You needn't do something** = it's not necessary to do it (but you can if you want). You can also use **don't/doesn't need to**. Note that we say *don't need to do*, but *needn't do* (without to).

examples.text: We have plenty of time. We **needn't hurry**.
examples.note: = it is not necessary to hurry

examples.text: Joe can stay here. He **needn't come** with us.
examples.note: = it is not necessary for him to come

left.label: needn't = it is not necessary
examples: You **needn't tell** Steve. I can tell him myself. (= it is not necessary)
We have plenty of time. We **needn't hurry**.

right.label: mustn't = don't do it
examples: You **mustn't tell** Steve. I don't want him to know. (= don't tell him)
We must be very quiet. We **mustn't make** any noise.

lesson.heading: needn't have (done)
lesson.text: Paul and Sarah reserved a table at a restaurant. But when they went to the restaurant, it was almost empty. *They **needn't have reserved** a table.* This means: they reserved a table, but now they know this was not necessary. Compare needn't (do) and needn't have (done).

examples.text: Everything will be OK. You **needn't worry**.
Everything was OK. You **needn't have worried**.
examples.note: you worried, but it was not necessary

lesson.heading: needn't have (done) or didn't need to (do)?

left.label: needn't have done = he did it, but it was not necessary
examples: Why did he get up at 5 o'clock? He **needn't have got up** so early. He could have stayed in bed longer.

right.label: didn't need to do = it was not necessary (whether he did it or not)
right.text: It doesn't matter whether he did it or not. You can also say He didn't have to get up.
examples: He **didn't need to get up** early, so he didn't.
He **didn't need to get up** early, but it was a beautiful morning, so he did.

lesson.text: needn't have done always means the person DID it (for nothing). If you only want to say it wasn't necessary, use didn't need to or didn't have to.

exercises.prompt: Match each sentence with must to the sentence with mustn't that has a similar meaning.

pairs.left: You must leave the furniture as it is.

exercises.prompt: I have to talk to Gary. I ___ remember to call him.
exercises.explanation: It is necessary that I remember: must.

exercises.prompt: Which phrase completes each sentence: mustn't or needn't / don't need to?

items.text: I have to talk to Gary. I ___ forget to call him.
There's plenty of time for you to decide. You ___ decide now.
These are important documents. We ___ lose them.
You ___ wait for me. You go on and I'll join you later.
This is a dangerous situation and we need to be careful. We ___ do anything stupid.
I understand the situation perfectly. You ___ explain further.

exercises.prompt: I can manage the shopping alone. You ___ with me.
exercises.explanation: It is not necessary for you to come: needn't come (without to).

exercises.prompt: I'll be all right. You ___ about me.
exercises.explanation: It is not necessary to worry: needn't worry.

exercises.statement: You needn't to shout. I can hear you perfectly.
exercises.explanation: You needn't shout (or You don't need to shout / You don't have to shout). Needn't is followed by the infinitive without to.

exercises.statement: This train is direct. You don't need to change.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Don't need to + infinitive = it is not necessary.

exercises.prompt: Why did you walk home? Why didn't you take a taxi? You ___ home. You could have taken a taxi.
exercises.explanation: You walked, but it was not necessary: needn't have + past participle.

exercises.prompt: Why did she phone me at 3 am? Why didn't she wait until the morning? Make a sentence with needn't have.
exercises.answer: She needn't have phoned me at 3 am.
exercises.explanation: She phoned, but it was not necessary: needn't have phoned.

exercises.prompt: Why did he get up at 5 o'clock? He ___ so early. He could have stayed in bed longer.
exercises.explanation: He got up, but it was not necessary: needn't have + past participle.

exercises.statement: You mustn't lock the door. It's OK to leave it unlocked.
exercises.explanation: You needn't lock the door (or You don't need to / don't have to lock the door). It is not necessary - mustn't would mean 'don't do it'.

exercises.statement: I needn't have said anything, so I kept quiet.
exercises.explanation: I didn't need to say anything (or I didn't have to say anything), so I kept quiet. Needn't have said would mean I did say something.
